## Skill Descriptions

**Sword** — In-game: *"Expertise with swords, rapiers, and the like. Swords are very damaging, and can reduce an opponent's Rage."* The wiki frames it as *"one of the first combat skills a new player finds… Sword focuses on damage and rage reduction, with a side of armor shred."* It requires a sword equipped in your main hand.

**Unarmed** — In-game: *"Mastery of the martial arts. Not especially damaging, but with great controlling and stunning abilities."* The wiki: *"Unarmed is a melee attack skill that focuses on crowd control and damage."* It generally requires one or both hands empty (Cestus/Claw are the exceptions).

So the descriptions already signal the difference: **Sword is the damage skill; Unarmed is the control/stun skill.**

## Damage Type

- **Sword:** Slashing (Sword Slash, Many Cuts, Finishing Blow, Decapitate, etc.) and Piercing (Thrusting Blade, Heart Piercer).
- **Unarmed:** Crushing (Punch, Headbutt, Bodyslam, Bruising Blow, etc.). It only gains Slashing-type hits from the Claw/Cestus line (Slashing Strike, Claw Barrage) at level 51+.

## Base PvE Damage Numbers (single-target, before gear/synergy)

| Level | Best Sword burst | Best Unarmed burst |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | **Decapitate — 100** | Bruising Blow 24 / Headbutt 41 |
| 30 | **Decapitate — 194** | Bodyslam 181 / Headbutt 86 |
| 50 | Decapitate 418 / Finishing Blow 270 | Bodyslam 569 / Headbutt 200 |
| 70 | **Decapitate — 761** | Bodyslam 569 / Headbutt 348 |
| 100 | **Decapitate — 1171** | Bodyslam 1170 |

**The gap widens the higher you level.** Sword's signature burst abilities (Decapitate, Finishing Blow) pull far ahead of Unarmed's Crushing hits for most of the skill's range — e.g. at level 70 Decapitate (761) nearly doubles Bodyslam (569).

## The One Convergence Point

Unarmed's heaviest hitter is **Bodyslam** (a huge 45-reset, 54–174 power-cost slam). It climbs steadily and **nearly ties Decapitate at level 100** — Bodyslam 1170 vs Decapitate 1171. That's the only place Unarmed's burst catches up, and it's a near-tie rather than a win.

## Summary

- **For raw single-target burst, Sword wins decisively** across almost the entire level range — its descriptions and numbers both confirm it's the damage skill.
- **Unarmed is a control skill** whose burst is modest until the very end, where Bodyslam finally matches Decapitate at level 100.
- **Costs:** Sword's big hits carry high power costs and long resets (Decapitate: 60s reset, 43–159 power; Finishing Blow: 20s reset, 24–101 power). Unarmed's Bodyslam is similarly expensive (45s reset, 54–174 power), while its smaller stuns (Headbutt 12s, Bruising Blow 10s) are cheap and utility-focused.

*(These are the abilities' base PvE damage values from the CDN — actual damage also scales with gear, skill level, and synergy bonuses.)*

## Sword Overview
Sword is typically one of the first combat skills a new player finds, along with Unarmed. Predictably, it requires a sword to be equipped in your main hand. Sword focuses on damage and rage reduction, with a side of armor shred. A well-geared swordsman can completely block a monster from using Rage attacks!

Calligraphy serves as the secondary skill for Sword, and provides various sword combos and special insights.

## In-Game Description
Expertise with swords, rapiers, and the like. Swords are very damaging, and can reduce an opponent's Rage.

## Training Sword

* New players learn/obtain Sword by picking up the starting backpack on Anagoge
* Nelson Ballard teaches Flashing Strike 1-4 and Precision Pierce 1-4
* Malvol teaches Decapitate 1-4, Thrusting Blade 1-4, and Heart Piercer 1-4
* Janet Lews will unlock levels 51-60, 61-70, and teaches level 51+ abilities
* Pegast will unlock levels 71-80, and teaches level 71+ abilities
* Levels 81-90 are unlocked by Emersil the Ever-Gloating deep beneath Povus.
* Sir Brooker will unlock levels 81-90, 91-100, Prodigy Potential, and teaches 90+ abilities.

## Unarmed Overview
Unarmed is a melee attack skill that focuses on crowd control and damage. Most abilities involve, punching, kicking, or throwing your opponent. 

Many Unarmed abilities will require you to actually be unarmed. This means no staff, beaker, bow, orb, flask, shield, etc. There are two exceptions: a Cestus (MainHand) or a Claw (OffHand). Neither of these will count as you being 'armed.' Animals can use all Unarmed abilities, but not if they have weapons (other than Cestus and Claw) equipped. Check Trivia at the bottom of page for exceptions to the above statement!
 

## In-Game Description
Mastery of the martial arts. Not especially damaging, but with great controlling and stunning abilities. Generally requires one or both hands to be empty, although you can use kicks even with other items wielded.

## Training Unarmed

All players start with Unarmed on Anagoge (the tutorial island). 

* Flia teaches Headbutt 1-3 and Bodyslam 1-3.
* Hogan teaches Mamba Strike 1-3 and Bruising Blow 1-3.
* Furlak will unlock levels 51-60, 61-70, and teaches level 51+ abilities.
* Pegast unlocks 71-80.
* Levels 81-90 are unlocked by Emersil the Ever-Gloating deep beneath Povus.
* Sir Hughes in Statehelm unlocks 81-90, 91-100, Prodigy Potential, and teaches level 80+ abilities.

## Secondary Skills:
* Meditation
: Meditation is Unarmed's secondary, or supplementary skill. Meditating at Meditation Pillars scattered around the world will give you the ability to use a certain combo, based on which recipe you use, as well one or two random combos that change daily. For example, the Level 3 Meditation recipe will grant "Combo: Fists of Rage". If you use Punch+Punch+Barrage in that order, the final step (Barrage) will deal 10 extra damage. 
: The duration of Meditation buffs can be extended by meditating on Meditation Stools, learned through Carpentry.

I have everything I need. Here's the full picture.

## Tending To the Root-Tenders

This is a **repeatable daily quest** from **Mope**, a myconian NPC in **Povus** who grows Iocaine and Coral mushrooms on the giant mushrooms. Mope asks you to protect his fungus from the ratkin root-tenders that keep trying to unearth it.

**Mope's dialogue:**
- *Pre-quest:* "You wish to aid me? Then exterminate the ratkin root-tenders that constantly try to unearth my fungus!"
- *On completion:* "I acknowledge your deeds, but still the ratkin attack! You have merely stunted their progress. But your efforts are noble nonetheless. Should you have the stomach to continue killing them, I would be grateful."

### Requirements
- **Favor:** Tolerated with Mope — **you already qualify.** Your favor with Mope is at **Friends** tier (well above the Tolerated gate).
- **Objectives:**
  1. **Kill Ratkin Root-Tenders ×10** (target: `RatkinRootTender`)
  2. **Talk to Mope ×1** (scripted)

### How to complete it
1. Talk to **Mope** in **Povus** to accept the quest.
2. Kill **10 Ratkin Root-Tenders**.
3. Return and **talk to Mope** to turn it in.

### Rewards
- **Xogrite Chunk ×3**
- **50 favor** with Mope

### Repeat schedule
- **Resets every 1 day.** After completion, Mope's line shifts to: *"If you were to exterminate more ratkin root-tenders, I would be in your debt,"* and you must wait a day before repeating.

**Note:** Your active quest log does not currently show this quest, so it isn't active right now — talk to Mope to pick it up. It's a good daily grind for Xogrite Chunks and favor.

Here's what I found about **The Wasted Wishes**.

## Overview
**The Wasted Wishes** is a **Lore Book** in the **Stories** category. It is a static in-game book found in a **house in Serbule**, and it belongs to the **Lore Books Library** (opened via the book-shaped icon on the right sidebar). Reading it earns **50 Lore XP** on first read.

## The story
The lorebook tells the tale of **Leeka**, who is confronted by a **gorgon** and forced into a series of wishes:

- **First wish (already spent):** The gorgon grants the first wish before Leeka even speaks — "That's the first wish used up already!"
- **Second wish:** Leeka demands to possess the blade **Heartseeker**, but adds hastily that it should *not* be impaled in her body — she wants it "safely in its scabbard, at my side." The gorgon grants it, and a weight appears at her side; it turns out to be her **mother's blade**, back in her hands at last.
- **Third (final) wish:** Leeka wishes for "the power to wield this sword in all its glory!" The gorgon responds with mockery: "You're a foolish litt[le]…"

The tale ends with Leeka opening her eyes — and closing them again just in time, because the gorgon was waiting right before her. It vanishes in a cloud of smoke, leaving the parting threat: **"Aw, almost got you... Don't worry, Leeka. I'll get you next time."**

## Key themes
The story is framed as a cautionary tale about gorgons — they manipulate you and won't take arguments ("No sense arguing with a gorgon; they would just manipulate you further"). It's a dark, deceptive encounter rather than a straightforward wish-granting.

## Notes
- The book is **extremely rare** and part of the work-in-progress Lore Books Library.
- No chat mentions or trade data exist for it (it's a lore document, not a tradeable item).
- The item itself isn't in the tradeable items table, consistent with it being a read-only lorebook.
